newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ANNOUNCES CONCESSIONS ON GAS PIPELINES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ANNOUNCES CONCESSIONS ON GAS PIPELINES.

text.p: Bulgaria on Tuesday officially announced offers for two pipeline concessions for transitting Russian gas through its territory and is expected to call two tenders within a month.
The two concession offers of 35 years each are for six existing transit gas pipelines and for five stretches planned to be built, said a government's decree published in the State Gazette.
The two concessions include the existing pipelines to Turkey, Greece and Macedonia and a pipeline to Serbia which is currently in design.
Bulgaria has 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country and currently transits Russian gas to Turkey and Greece.
Its pipeline to Macedonia has been constructed and filled with gas but is still waiting for its western neighbours to complete the pipeline on their territory.
Another stretch from the southwestern town of Dupnitsa to the border with Serbia near the Kalotina checkpoint is currently in design.
Petar Sabev, executive director of Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas said last week that the company had already purchased the needed pipelines for the link to Serbia and they were on site.

The winner of the tender for enlarging the gas transit system on Bulgarian territory, which is expected to cost some $500 million, will operate it under the formula build-operate-transfer, government officials said.
The tender winner should supply Russian gas on preferential prices and part of the volumes should be delivered against Bulgarian goods and services, said the State Gazette.
Trade minister Atanas Paparizov said last month Bulgaria has already prepared a list of goods and services to be supplied to Russia against part of the gas.

Bulgaria's cabinet decided to offer the two pipeline concessions on December 29 and the head of concession department Nikola Baltov said the tenders' winners would be announced within three months after launching the tenders.
Participants in the two tenders should present a banking guarantee of $5 million.

The Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up last year by Gazprom and Bulgargas, is considered as a serious candidate for the concessions, energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said.
Gazprom has 50 percent in Topenergy and Bulgargas holds a 25.1 percent stake. The remaining 24.9 percent are distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
